Iqbal never wrote the shaheen as an ornament. He wrote it as an instruction — a bird that is defined by where it is willing to go next. Allama Muhammad Iqbal

He named five habits worth borrowing: it flies highest, it keeps its own company, it eats only what it kills, it sees further than the flock, and it builds no nest. That last one is the hard one. Comfort is the thing that grounds you.

03 — Different legends. Same sky.

Our legends

Not characters we play. Qualities we play like.

Strength is not in the weapon, but in the will to rise again. The Shaheen creed
Bödvar
Foundation

Where everyone starts and most people stop. Learn spacing and recovery on him and it transfers to every legend after.

Orion
Precision

Spacing is the entire character. A pixel too close is a whiff, a pixel too far is a free punish.

Val
Control

Every string is a decision tree. She rewards the player who already knows their next three inputs.

Brynn
Strength

Meet force with force. Hold the centre of the map, make them come to you, and punish the moment they do.

Teros
Punishment

He doesn't chase. He waits for the panic and makes one grab count for the whole stock.

Asuri
Speed

Close the distance before they've finished the thought. Hesitation is the only thing that kills her.

Dusk
Timing

Nothing lands early, nothing lands late. He's proof that patience beats reflexes more often than not.

Vector
Pursuit

There is nowhere on the map that counts as away. Recover, re-engage, and take the ledge back.

Thor
Momentum

Once it starts rolling, don't give it a reason to stop. Every hit should buy the next one.

Mordex
Relentless

Pressure that never lets up. He doesn't out-think you, he out-lasts you, and most players break before the clock does.

Nix
Adaptability

Read the lobby, change the plan. Same player in game three as game one, with an entirely different answer.

Jaeyun
Resolve

Down a stock and still calm. Nothing is decided until the last life is gone, and he plays like he knows it.

Tezca
Power

One opening is the whole match. Commit completely or don't commit — half a read is worse than no read.
